title: Bhai Kanhaiya Gives Water to Both Sides
text:
Sikh tradition remembers Bhai Kanhaiya, a devoted follower of Guru Gobind Singh, as a water carrier. During the battles around the Sikh stronghold of Anandpur, in the early 1700s, he went among the wounded with a leather water bag, giving drink to the injured and dying.

Some Sikh soldiers noticed that he gave water to wounded Mughal and hill soldiers as well as to their own men, and that some of those he revived went back to fight. They complained to the Guru that Kanhaiya was helping the enemy.

Guru Gobind Singh called him and asked if this was true. According to the tradition, Kanhaiya replied that he saw no friend or enemy on the field. He saw only the Guru's face in every man who cried out for water. The Guru was pleased. He gave Kanhaiya a balm and told him to dress the wounds of the injured as well as give them water.

Sikhs see Bhai Kanhaiya as an example of selfless service, and some describe him as a forerunner of the idea later embodied by the Red Cross. Sikh volunteer groups that serve all victims of war and disaster honor his name.
lesson: Compassion for someone in pain need not ask which side they are on. Helping without distinction is the purest form of service.
source: Sikh tradition, recorded in later Sikh histories and sakhis (traditional stories)
caveat: The episode comes from Sikh tradition and is not documented in contemporary records.
